## Project overview

This project implements an AI-enhanced anti-money-laundering (AML) transaction
monitoring and investigation system, deployed as an interactive
[Streamlit application](https://data-science-in-financial-service-project.streamlit.app/).
It is designed for the bank's middle office and validated on the IBM AML
LI-Small synthetic dataset of 234,534 accounts and 250,000 transactions, at a
2.26 % suspicious-account prevalence.

The system is a **prioritisation overlay** on top of existing rules, not a
replacement detector: the rules continue to define the population that must be
reviewed (preserving regulatory coverage), while a combined AI risk score
re-ranks that population so investigators reach genuine cases first. All final
decisions remain with qualified human investigators, in alignment with MAS
Notice 626 and the MAS FEAT framework.

## Detection pipeline

A three-layer pipeline produces a single weighted risk score per account:

- **Rule engine** — 10 MAS Notice 626-aligned deterministic checks producing
  auditable, threshold-based evidence.
- **XGBoost classifier** — trained on 35 behavioural and network features,
  achieving AUC-ROC 0.856 / AUC-PR 0.186 on a 30 % held-out test set.
- **Leiden community detection** — partitions the transaction graph into 69,878
  communities, scoring each account on cluster suspicious density, size, and
  internal transaction intensity.

The three signals are combined — 50 % XGBoost, 25 % community detection, 25 %
rules — into a 0–100 risk score that prioritises high-risk accounts for review.
SHAP values provide per-account explainability.

## Results

Measured on the held-out test set (30 % of 234,534 accounts):

| Detection method | Alerts | Precision | Recall | F1 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Rules only | 14,800 | 2.3 % | 21.4 % | 4.2 % |
| XGBoost (optimised) | 1,992 | 22.1 % | 27.7 % | 24.6 % |
| Community detection | 3,926 | 12.0 % | 29.7 % | 17.2 % |
| **Combined AI system** | **1,172** | **31.8 %** | **23.4 %** | **27.0 %** |

The combined system raises top-queue precision from 2.3 % to 31.8 % — roughly a
14× improvement — while shrinking the deep-review queue by about 92 %. Reviewing
the top 100 ranked accounts surfaces 85 true suspicious accounts versus 13 under
rule-severity ordering, an estimated saving on the order of 3,400
investigator-hours per monitoring cycle.

## Investigation copilot

A scripted generative-AI layer — implemented as a fully offline, reproducible
simulation requiring no external model or API key — provides on-demand
investigation briefs, Suspicious Transaction Report (STR) drafts, and an
investigator copilot, grounded entirely in the predictive-AI output.
